title: Prove the pure dual-pair retirement criterion and its unit-divisor count (no κ)
body:
**No new κ.** The package states and proves when one independent input of an equal-target class can be retired at a cut: over the dyadic ring, a retirement (basis change on the class at the start and end, basis change on the combinable registers at the cut, pivot register emitted and reloaded with a fresh input) exists exactly when there is a pure dual pair `P c = s u`, `a P = s d`, `a u = 1`. The completion to ordinary events is explicit over `Z[1/2]`; `d c = 1` already splits the class, so no separate primitive-vector condition is needed.

Also proved: ordinary events leave the pairing unchanged (only cuts after non-ordinary events matter); the number of simultaneous retirements of one job is the number of unit elementary divisors of the pairing, not its rank over `Q` (an explicit rank-one pairing with divisor 3 admits none); inside native calls, helper classes see only the native block, caller classes reduce to the caller cut before the call, and consecutive calls never share a pair (the statement stops at interleaved calls).

Exact checks on the literal words, with the retired word replayed from a freshly computed completion each time:
- #6716 unretired caller: the only pair is at cut 353 (class {4,20,21}); #6726 unretired caller: pairs at cuts 158, 383, 392; #6726 final caller (the caller of #6805): no pair at any cut.
- #6805 native word with the retimed move: cut 12372, frame 243, helper 368; pure rows exist only with the retimed role in the frame; Gram `[4,4,4,4]`, a unit of `Z[1/2]` but not of `Z`; retired endpoint checked on all 771 public inputs.
- Controls: pivot outside the class, non-pure row, non-pure column, zero pairing, frame without the retimed role, word without the retiming, rank one without a unit.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a. Inputs are unmodified copies pinned in `retained/SOURCE-PINS.json` and `SOURCES.json` to #6716 at 4a40713f10d47da5894d7673eb6d0ab2ebdf0687, #6726 at 435bbe91fb28cb1d7a569ca70c6c4e9eb302d486 and #6805 at 0ecd4fd79f4f7fc21b2ef7a9cdc73912fa4a804b.

Reproduce (CPython 3.12, standard library):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-dual-pair-retirement-criterion
```
Expected: `PASS_DUAL_PAIR_RETIREMENT_CRITERION` (normal and `-O`) and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Scope: retirements of the conjugation type defined in `PROOF.md` section 1; equal-target classes with block-diagonal endpoint; scalars `Z[1/2]` (the same proof covers `Z[i][1/2]`, not executed); the level section uses an explicit block model; classes mixing caller roles with helper inputs and interleaved calls are not covered. Pricing, native phases and the five framework assumptions of the cited words are not re-derived and no κ changes.

Overlap: #6764 states the pair conditions as a necessary interface for the binary full-bank model; Ali Romman's helper-basis completion supplies the `a b = 1` completion step. This package gives the general equivalence with the converse, the unit-divisor count and the level propositions.
